newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to charge leading Socialists with corruption.
newsitem.headline: Spain to charge leading Socialists with corruption.

text.p: Spain's Supreme Court has decided to charge 26 people, among them top officials in the former ruling Socialist party, with corruption, court documents published on Friday said.

Guillermo Galeote, former finance director for the Socialist Workers' Party, and accounts director Aida Alvarez, were among those to be charged in the Filesa party financing corruption case, the court documents said.
Seven people including two former Socialist parliamentarians have already been accused in the Filesa case, named after a front-company set up to channel funds to the party.
The court also decided, in a meeting early on Friday, not to try any bankers or financiers in the case.

The state prosecutor had said 10 Spanish companies paid more than 1.08 billion pesetas ($8.7 million) to several front companies, set up by those who are to stand trial, for bogus studies and reports. In return they received government favours.
The scandal, which came to light three years ago, embarrassed the former Socialist government and contributed to its election defeat in March after 13 years in power.
